name: Obbattu (Holige)
instructions: 1. Soak chana dal and pressure cook until soft, then drain excess water.
2. In a pan, combine cooked dal and jaggery; cook until moisture evaporates, forming a thick consistency called 'hoorana'.
3. Add cardamom and nutmeg powder to the hoorana and let it cool.
4. Prepare a soft, elastic dough using maida, water, oil, and a pinch of turmeric.
5. Take a small portion of dough, flatten it, place a ball of hoorana inside, and seal the edges.
6. Gently roll the stuffed ball into a thin, round disc using a plastic sheet or parchment paper coated with oil.
7. Roast on a hot tawa with a teaspoon of ghee until golden brown spots appear on both sides.
description: Obbattu, also known as Holige or Puran Poli, is a quintessential Karnataka delicacy. It is a mandatory festive treat, particularly during Ugadi and Varamahalakshmi Vratam, symbolizing prosperity and sweetness in family life.
